plan.title: COP31 Ends Without a Deal: What Happened and What's Next
plan.description: COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, ended on 22 November 2026 without an overarching climate pact after divisions over fossil fuels and finance. This video summarizes the outcomes, the progress that was made, and what experts say comes next.

beats.narration: Two weeks of talks. Two extra days of overtime. And still no deal. The longest climate summit in history just ended in Antalya, and the world is leaving without a pact.
beats.chapter: A summit that ran out of time

beats.narration: The summit began on November 9 with almost 200 nations. It followed a summer of record heat, landslides and wildfires, and a major El Niño was expected to make things worse.
It closed Sunday at 7:33 in the evening, almost 50 hours late. President Murat Kurum said he leaves the deadlock to the judgement of the entire world and humanity.

props.text: I leave the deadlock of the negotiations to the judgement of the entire world and humanity.

beats.narration: The sticking point was fossil fuels. Countries argued over whether the final decision should repeat the call to transition away from them, and some feared it leaned too hard on carbon capture.
Money was the other fight. Negotiators could not agree on a specific dollar figure for climate finance, which left developing countries without the support that a phaseout would need.

props.label: Yearly adaptation need for developing countries by 2035 (UNEP)

beats.narration: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called the result deeply disappointing, and said there is no ambiguity in the science.

headlines.text: COP31 ends without climate pact as UN chief warns there is ‘no ambiguity in the science’

beats.narration: The World Resources Institute went further. It called the outcome hollow, a failure of political leadership, but not a failure of the Paris Agreement itself.

props.text: A failure of political leadership, not of the Paris Agreement.

beats.narration: Not everything failed. The UN climate body says nations reached agreements on a Just Transition, climate finance, adaptation, technology, transparency and the second global stocktake.
The Action Agenda also saw real-economy progress, including a major boost for electrification. The European Investment Bank is targeting over 30 billion euros for adaptation between 2026 and 2030.

Outside the formal talks, participants set up a plurilateral process, where willing countries cooperate in smaller groups. A follow-up conference will be held in Tuvalu in 2027, co-hosted with Ireland.
The science is urgent. In October, the UN Environment Programme warned emissions must fall nearly a fifth within four years, and close to half within a decade, to avoid a disastrous overshoot.

props.title: The science is urgent. In October, the UN Environment

beats.narration: There is a small bright spot. Carbon Brief reports fossil CO2 emissions may fall about 0.4 percent in 2026, driven by an oil drop and the energy shock from the Iran conflict. Coal is still rising slightly.

Experts at the Atlantic Council describe fragmenting climate governance, with plurilateral cooperation as a way to keep progress alive. Public support may help: in all 18 countries surveyed, adults say methane action would improve their view of leaders.
The takeaway: the Paris Agreement still stands, but the talks failed on fossil fuels and finance. Progress now depends on coalitions of willing countries, and on leaders acting at home.

props.text: The talks failed. The need to act did not go away.

accuracy.reason: Most claims track the notes, but 'longest climate summit in history' and 'the world is leaving without a pact' are stretched, and the $305B stat is used beside a finance-failure claim it does not support. The notes also contain internal inconsistencies, such as UN News listing the conference as Nov 9-20 and ENB saying it ended almost 50 hours late.

coverage.reason: It covers the COP31 collapse, the causes, what was agreed, and the next steps. But the request asked for major national announcements (NDCs, EU or US moves), and none appear. Expert views are thin.

structure.reason: The chapters run in a clean order from what happened to why, what was done, and what comes next, ending on a takeaway. Beats 2 and 3 are slightly padded, and the 'what's next' section is weak.

hook_ending.reason: 'Two weeks of talks. Two extra days of overtime. And still no deal.' is a punchy open. The ending is a clear takeaway, though a little summary-like.

tone.reason: The neutral, newsy register suits a US adult audience. It attributes quotes and does not editorialize.

visuals.reason: The scene variety is good. But beat 11 is a title scene with a truncated sentence as its title, the $305B stat does not match the narration about finance failing, the 'Tuvalu' map is vague, and the gallery has generic queries.

originality.reason: It includes specifics such as the 7:33pm close, the Kurum quote and the methane poll. Otherwise it is mostly a standard news recap.

instructions.reason: It is about the right length and in English, and it gives an as-of date on the title. It omits national announcements, which were explicitly requested, and 'experts say next' is thin.
